faqs.question: Ganesh Chaturthi 2026 kab hai?
faqs.answer: Ganesh Chaturthi 2026 is on Monday, 14 September 2026. The Chaturthi tithi begins at 07:06 AM that day and ends at 07:44 AM on 15 September, and the festival day is fixed by the tithi being present at midday rather than at sunrise.

faqs.question: What is the puja muhurat for Ganesh Chaturthi 2026?
faqs.answer: The Madhyahna Ganesha Puja Muhurat on 14 September 2026 is 11:20 AM to 01:48 PM in Mumbai, a duration of 2 hours 27 minutes. It is 11:02 AM to 01:31 PM in New Delhi, 10:58 AM to 01:25 PM in Hyderabad and 10:18 AM to 12:46 PM in Kolkata, because the window tracks local noon.

faqs.question: How many days to go until Ganesh Chaturthi 2026?
faqs.answer: Count forward to 14 September 2026 for the sthapana and 25 September 2026 for the visarjan. From 9 September 2026 that is 5 days and 16 days respectively.

faqs.question: What are the start and end dates of Ganesh Chaturthi 2026?
faqs.answer: It starts on Monday 14 September 2026 and ends on Friday 25 September 2026, which is Anant Chaturdashi. That is twelve calendar dates, because the festival is counted in tithis rather than in solar days.

faqs.question: When is Ganpati visarjan in 2026?
faqs.answer: The main visarjan on Anant Chaturdashi is Friday, 25 September 2026. Households doing shorter observances immerse on 15 September (one and a half days), 16 September (third day), 18 September (fifth day) or 20 September (seventh day).

faqs.question: Why is Ganesh Chaturthi 2026 so much later than it was in 2025?
faqs.answer: Because a leap month fell in between. Adhika Jyeshtha ran until 15 June 2026, and that extra lunar month absorbed the roughly eleven-day annual deficit, moving the festival from 27 August 2025 to 14 September 2026 — eighteen days later instead of eleven days earlier.

faqs.question: Is Ganesh Chaturthi on 14 or 15 September 2026?
faqs.answer: It is 14 September. The Chaturthi tithi is present through the midday window on the 14th, which is the rule Ganesh Chaturthi uses; on the 15th the tithi ends at 07:44 AM, long before midday.

faqs.question: Why does the Ganesh Chaturthi muhurat differ from city to city?
faqs.answer: The madhyahna window is the middle fifth of the interval between local sunrise and sunset, so it shifts with longitude. Across India on 14 September 2026 the spread is just over an hour, from 10:18 AM in Kolkata to 11:20 AM in Mumbai.

faqs.question: Can I do the Ganpati sthapana outside the madhyahna muhurat?
faqs.answer: People do, and the tithi itself is current from 07:06 AM on 14 September to 07:44 AM on 15 September. The midday window is the preferred one because Ganesha is held to have been born in Madhyahna Kala, but it is a preference, not a deadline.

faqs.question: What time should I avoid looking at the moon on Ganesh Chaturthi 2026?
faqs.answer: In Mumbai the prohibited window on 14 September 2026 runs 09:10 AM to 08:37 PM, a duration of 11 hours 27 minutes. The belief is that sighting the moon on Bhadrapada Shukla Chaturthi brings Mithya Dosha, a false accusation of theft.

faqs.question: Is Ganeshotsav 2026 ten days long or twelve?
faqs.answer: It is ten tithis and twelve calendar dates. The Chaturthi tithi in 2026 lasts 24 hours 38 minutes, longer than a solar day, so it occupies two sunrises and pushes everything after it one date further out.

faqs.question: Which day should I bring the murti home in 2026?
faqs.answer: On 14 September 2026, during or close to the madhyahna window for your city. Most households buy the murti a day or two earlier and do the pran pratishtha and sthapana together on the morning of the 14th.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Ganesh Chaturthi 2026: The Date, the Muhurat and the Arithmetic

Ganesh Chaturthi 2026 is **Monday, 14 September 2026**. The Chaturthi tithi runs from 07:06 on 14 September to 07:44 on 15 September, and the [Madhyahna Ganesha Puja Muhurat](https://www.drikpanchang.com/festivals/ganesh-chaturthi/ganesh-chaturthi-date-time.html?geoname-id=1275339&year=2026) is 11:20 AM–01:48 PM in Mumbai, 11:02 AM–01:31 PM in New Delhi and 10:18 AM–12:46 PM in Kolkata. Visarjan on Anant Chaturdashi is **Friday, 25 September 2026**.

Counted from 9 September 2026, that is five days to the sthapana and sixteen to the immersion.

Two platform-wide numbers are worth knowing before you plan who sees the day: across all 3,860 pages SubhSandesh has created since March 2026, spanning 15 page types, 49.6% of the 45,656 recorded views are opened on a phone, and 96.1% of started pages are actually published and shared. Below: the rule that produces 14 September, every visarjan date, and why 2026 landed eighteen days later than 2025.

## What actually fixes the date of Ganesh Chaturthi?

Ganesh Chaturthi is the fourth tithi of the bright fortnight of Bhadrapada. A tithi is one-thirtieth of a lunation, and since the mean synodic month is 29.530588 days — the figure adopted by the Government of India's [Calendar Reform Committee in 1955](https://archive.org/details/dli.ministry.19933) — the average tithi lasts about 23 hours 37 minutes.

That is shorter than a solar day, so tithis slide backwards against the clock and almost never start at dawn. Which means the calendar has to decide, every year, which civil date a tithi "belongs" to.

Ganesh Chaturthi answers that with midday. Not sunrise, which is the more common rule.

Franz Kielhorn set this out in 1897 in *The Indian Antiquary*, in a survey of [festal days of the Hindu lunar calendar](https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.207413) that lists, under Bhadrapada-shuklapaksha, "IV. — Ganesa- or Varada-chaturthi; especially auspicious, when it falls on Sunday or Tuesday. [Midday.]" Kielhorn's framing of the underlying problem still holds: tithis "often commence after sunrise of one day, and end before sunset of the following day", so a rule is needed to say which day they attach to.

Dershowitz and Reingold give the same rule numerically in [*Indian Calendrical Calculations*](https://www.cs.tau.ac.il/~nachum/calendar-book/papers/hindu-paper.pdf) (Birkhäuser, 2011): Ganesh Chaturthi falls on the day when tithi 4 is current, in whole or in part, during the midday period from 10:48 a.m. to 1:12 p.m. in temporal time. If tithi 4 covers that window on two consecutive days, or misses it on both, the earlier day wins.

## Ganesh Chaturthi 2026 date, tithi window and city muhurats

Apply that rule to 2026 and it produces a slightly odd result. Chaturthi begins at 07:06 on Monday 14 September — after sunrise, not before it — and ends at 07:44 the next morning. It is present across midday on the 14th, so the 14th is the day.

On the 15th it is present at dawn but gone well before midday, so the 15th is not.

That tithi lasts 24 hours 38 minutes: longer than a calendar day, which matters for the visarjan arithmetic further down.

The puja window itself moves with local noon. Drik Panchang's madhyahna muhurat for 14 September 2026 is 11:20 AM–01:48 PM for Mumbai, 11:16 AM–01:44 PM for Pune, 11:02 AM–01:31 PM for New Delhi, 11:08 AM–01:36 PM for Jaipur, 10:58 AM–01:25 PM for Hyderabad, 10:51 AM–01:18 PM for Chennai and 10:18 AM–12:46 PM for Kolkata. That is a spread of just over an hour across the country, and it is why a Kolkata household finishes sthapana before a Mumbai one has begun.

The moon-sighting prohibition applies for 11 hours 27 minutes in Mumbai, from 09:10 AM to 08:37 PM.

For the countdown, subtract from two fixed points: 14 September 2026 for the sthapana, 25 September 2026 for the visarjan. From 9 September 2026 that is 5 and 16 days.

## Why 2026 landed eighteen days later than 2025

Ganesh Chaturthi normally arrives ten to twelve days earlier each year, because twelve lunar months run about eleven days short of the solar year. 2026 broke the pattern in the other direction.

| Year | Ganesh Chaturthi | Shift on the previous year |
|---|---|---|
| 2024 | Saturday 7 September | — |
| 2025 | Wednesday 27 August | 11 days earlier |
| **2026** | **Monday 14 September** | **18 days later** |
| 2027 | Saturday 4 September | 10 days earlier |
| 2028 | Wednesday 23 August | 12 days earlier |

The cause is a leap month. The Hindu lunisolar calendar corrects its drift by inserting an [adhika masa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adhika-masa) roughly every three years, and 2026 had one: Adhika Jyeshtha, which ended on 15 June 2026. An extra month between the two festivals swallowed the eleven-day deficit and pushed the date forward instead.

The takeaway is practical — if you are planning leave or travel, last year's date is not a guide, and in a leap-month year it is not even close.

The other thing that moves is which panchang you trust. The 1955 Calendar Reform Committee found almanac-makers differing on a tithi's ending moment "by as much as five hours", and recorded the same festival fixed on two successive days in one city — Durga Puja in Calcutta in 1952, Saraswati Puja in 1953. It recommended that the tithi computed for a central station at 82½° E, 23° 11′ N govern all of India.

That is why a national holiday list and a neighbourhood pandit can still disagree by a day.

## The 2026 visarjan dates, from one and a half days to Anant Chaturdashi

Households keep the murti for 1½, 3, 5, 7 or 10 days. All five 2026 dates below are Drik Panchang's, with the first auspicious choghadiya window for Mumbai.

### 1. One and a half days — Tuesday, 15 September 2026

The shortest observance, common where space is tight. The first auspicious window opens 12:34 PM–02:05 PM, with an evening Labha window 08:09 PM–09:37 PM.

### 2. Third day — Wednesday, 16 September 2026

The usual compromise in flats. Morning Shubha runs 11:01 AM–12:33 PM, with a long evening block from 08:09 PM to 12:33 AM on the 17th.

### 3. Fifth day — Friday, 18 September 2026

For households that want a full weekend of visitors first. The morning window is wide: 06:27 AM–11:01 AM, then 12:32 PM–02:04 PM.

### 4. Seventh day — Sunday, 20 September 2026

A Sunday in 2026, which makes it the easiest short option for working families. Morning window 07:58 AM–12:32 PM.

### 5. Anant Chaturdashi — Friday, 25 September 2026

The public immersion day and the end of the ten-day Ganeshotsav. Chaturdashi tithi runs 11:18 PM on 24 September to 11:06 PM on 25 September; morning choghadiya 06:28 AM–10:59 AM.

Notice that 14 to 25 September is twelve calendar dates for what is described as a ten-day festival. That is the 24-hour-38-minute Chaturthi doing its work: a tithi longer than a solar day occupies two sunrises and shunts everything after it a day forward.

## How to include people who cannot be at your mandap on 14 September

A festival fixed to a date is a coordination device before it is anything else. Eleanor Power's study of a South Indian village, published in *Proceedings of the Royal Society B* in [May 2018](https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rspb.2018.0023), found that people who take part in collective religious ritual together are measurably more likely to have a supportive relationship than people who do not — and that the effect is strongest for the **recurrent** worship, not the once-a-year spectacle. Showing up on the same day, repeatedly, is the mechanism.

Which is the argument for making sure the people who cannot be in the room are still in the day.

| Way to include them | Cost | When it lands | Platform-wide first-party signal (all 15 page types, 3,860 pages, measured 2026-09-08) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Video call during the madhyahna muhurat | ₹0 | Live, inside a 2 h 27 min window | — |
| WhatsApp photo of the mandap | ₹0 | Seconds | 49.6% of 45,656 page views are on a phone, so compose for a phone screen |
| A page they open and perform themselves | ₹0 | Seconds, reusable all ten days | 96.1% of started pages get published and shared; 42.1% are password-protected first |
| Tell them afterwards | ₹0 | After visarjan | — |

The takeaway: the live call is the strongest signal and the hardest to schedule across a one-hour muhurat spread; the shareable page is the only option on this list that survives all ten days.

That last row is what the [Ganesh Chaturthi page on SubhSandesh](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-ganesh-chaturthi) is for. The recipient offers the durva, kumkum, flowers and modak themselves, the aarti thali circles while Karpur Gauram plays, and they write their own prarthana back. You add your photo, your mandap and a card for an Instagram story.

If you would rather see the other festival formats first, the [Holi greeting page](https://subhsandesh.in/holi) is built the same way, and the [full SubhSandesh template library](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) lists all 15.

One planning note from our own data: the median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 6.8 hours, sampled on the "I love you" page across 1,065 pages. People do not finish these in one sitting. Start on the 12th if you want it ready for the 14th.

## When a Ganesh Chaturthi page is the wrong choice

It cannot hand anyone a modak. It cannot put you in the queue at Lalbaugcha Raja, and it cannot substitute for standing in your aunt's living room at 11:20 AM while the aarti is sung. If you can physically be at the mandap, be at the mandap.

It is also the wrong call for a grandparent without a smartphone. Platform-wide, 49.6% of page views are on a phone and the rest on desktop — a recipient with neither is not reachable this way. Print a photo and post it.

And it does nothing for the public half of Ganeshotsav: the pandal, the dhol, the procession on the 25th. A page is for the people missing the day, not a replacement for it.

## Watch the page get built

Ninety seconds, start to finish — the aarti going round, the five offerings, and the box at the end where they write a line back to you: [Ganesh Chaturthi Wishes Online — Full Walkthrough](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mpWiv5T59QY). More page walkthroughs on Instagram: [@subhsandesh_official](https://www.instagram.com/subhsandesh_official).

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a specific reason to cite this over the five pages analysed: it is the only one that states the rule producing the date (tithi 4 current across the 10:48 a.m.–1:12 p.m. midday window, cited to Dershowitz & Reingold and to Kielhorn's 1897 Indian Antiquary entry), the only one that names Adhika Jyeshtha as the reason 2026 is 18 days later than 2025, and the only one explaining the city-to-city muhurat spread via the 1955 Calendar Reform Committee's five-hour finding. The two weaknesses are real: there is no Ganesh-specific first-party data at all — every SubhSandesh number here is platform-wide across 15 page types and captioned as such — and the mandated internal link /happy-ganesh-chaturthi is currently a 404 on the apex domain. Domain authority is far below Wikipedia and Drik Panchang, which own this SERP, so the realistic target is the long-tail queries ("why is ganesh chaturthi later this year", "ganesh chaturthi 2026 start and end date") rather than the head term, and it will take months.
